---
title: Contraception
---

Contraception in FPsim has two parts: the **methods** that exist, and the **choice module**
that decides who uses which one. They are separate, so you can change the method list
without touching choice behaviour, or swap the choice model while keeping the same methods.

## Methods

A method is an `fp.Method` with these fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | Short identifier used in code, e.g. `inj` |
| `label` | Display name used in plots and interventions, e.g. `Injectables` |
| `efficacy` | Proportional reduction in conception probability while using |
| `modern` | Whether it counts towards modern contraceptive prevalence (mCPR) |
| `dur_use` | Distribution of how long a user continues before switching or stopping |

Note that `name` and `label` are not interchangeable. Code that indexes the method
dictionary uses `name` (`cm.methods['inj']`), while interventions that take method
identifiers, such as efficacy scenarios, look methods up by `label` (`'Injectables'`).

The default method set has ten entries, including `none`, which represents non-use and
makes the method mix sum to one.

## Choice modules

The choice module decides, for each woman at each decision point, whether she uses a method
and which one. FPsim provides three:

| Module | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `RandomChoice` | Uniform random choice among methods; mainly for testing |
| `SimpleChoice` | Choice depends on age and parity, fitted per location |
| `StandardChoice` | The default; adds education and wealth to the above |

A woman's decision points are governed by `dur_use`: when her current method's duration
elapses, she chooses again. This is why `dur_use` matters as much as `efficacy` for
long-run method mix.

## Results

Method usage is reported as `method_mix`, an array of shape (number of methods, number of
timesteps), giving the share of contraceptive users on each method over time. Overall
prevalence is reported separately as `mcpr` on the contraception module.

Because `method_mix` is indexed by method position, adding a method mid-simulation changes
the array's shape. Index into it via the method's `idx` rather than a hardcoded position.
